record.context_brief: circle actions on positively curved manifolds
record.original_question: If a manifold M has positive sectional curvature, must it admit a faithful S^1-action? If such an action exists, must it be isometric for some positively curved metric?

evidence.quote: Question 4.2. If a manifold \(M\) has positive sectional curvature, does it admit a faithful \(\mathbf{S}^1\) action? This being the case, is the action isometric?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a closed smooth manifold that admits a Riemannian metric of positive sectional curvature (i.e., for every point $p \in M$ and every $2$-plane $\sigma \subset T_pM$, the sectional curvature $K(\sigma) > 0$). A smooth action of the circle group $S^1$ on $M$ is called faithful if the homomorphism $S^1 \to \mathrm{Diff}(M)$ defining it is injective. The action is called isometric with respect to a Riemannian metric $g$ on $M$ if $S^1$ acts by $g$-isometries.

(a) Must $M$ admit a faithful smooth $S^1$-action?

(b) If $M$ admits a faithful smooth $S^1$-action, must this action be isometric with respect to some Riemannian metric on $M$ of positive sectional curvature?
artifact.status_search_result: The classification of positively curved manifolds with symmetry (the Grove symmetry program) remains a very active area, with strong partial results when an isometric torus action of sufficiently high rank is assumed (Hsiang–Kleiner, Grove–Searle, Wilking, etc.), but no general result asserting that every positively curved closed manifold admits a faithful (let alone isometric) circle action is known. Surveys by Ziller and others list the existence of symmetries on positively curved manifolds among the central open problems. No solution to this question was found.

status_evidence.title: Riemannian Manifolds with Positive Sectional Curvature (Ziller)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing how little is known about general positively curved manifolds and the role of symmetry assumptions, with the existence of symmetries listed as a guiding open problem.
status_evidence.claim: The question of which positively curved manifolds admit (isometric) symmetries remains open in general.

status_evidence.title: Positive curvature, symmetry, and topology
status_evidence.snippet: Recent survey on the symmetry program for positively curved manifolds, summarizing partial results assuming isometric torus actions.
status_evidence.claim: No general theorem ensures the existence of a faithful or isometric S^1-action on every positively curved manifold.
